claim_limit: This is an evidence matrix for eight already-adjudicated included families in a partial retrieval. It does not estimate ecosystem prevalence, artifact-availability prevalence, or certification-practice prevalence.

records.title: Adaptive Branch Specialization in Spectral-Spatial Graph Neural Networks for Certified Robustness

evidence.finding: The paper derives a fused-output perturbation bound from branch and gate Lipschitz quantities.
The numerical results report clean and attack accuracy (DropEdge, Metattack, and Feature-PGD); no per-input certified radius or certified-accuracy evaluation of Theorem 4 was located.

The certificate uses analytic branch bounds from Chebyshev coefficients, input norms, layer spectral-norm bounds, and a spectral-norm product for the gate. This coding concerns the stated analytic protocol, conditional on its premises; the paper does not numerically instantiate it.
The link returned HTTP 403 at audit, so no public checkpoint could be inspected. No author contact was authorized.

evidence.locator: p. 1 code footnote and reproducibility checklist
evidence.finding: The paper points to an anonymous repository, but that official link was inaccessible at audit; executable certificate code could not be located in the inspectable official sources.

undecidable_or_unoperationalized_premise: The spatial-branch premise that the attention derivative norm is at most one is assumed but no artifact-level checking procedure is supplied.
The inaccessible paper-linked artifact prevents evaluating the learned-model-specific constants and margins.

evidence.finding: Several weight/filter quantities are directly computable, but at least one analytic premise is assumed and the artifact cannot be inspected.
The official paper-linked artifact was not inspectable at the cutoff, so an artifact/theorem semantic comparison could not be performed.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Node-wise, channel-wise sigmoid context gate over two branches.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: Not a top-k selector; continuous two-branch interpolation.
semantics.logit_probability_or_margin_output: A linear classifier consumes the fused representation; training loss applies softmax.
semantics.preprocessing_and_perturbation_units: Joint l0 edge flips p and l-infinity feature perturbation epsilon (Eq. (15)).
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Node/fused-output bound under the stated joint perturbation set, conditional on global branch and gate bounds.

records.title: BALANCING ACCURACY AND ROBUSTNESS IN INTRUSION DETECTION: AN ENSEMBLE DEEP LEARNING APPROACH

evidence.finding: The paper reports sigma=0.25, 200 Monte Carlo samples, and a final-classifier certified robustness radius of 0.48.
The smoothing noise and sample count are stated, but the full confidence-bound/significance protocol needed to audit the reported certified radius was not located.
The official record contains the paper PDF and no model checkpoint. No author contact was authorized.

evidence.locator: record file list and linked resources
evidence.finding: The paper specifies the smoothing classifier in Eq. (11), but the official record exposes no executable certificate implementation.

undecidable_or_unoperationalized_premise: The confidence interval, failure probability, and class-probability estimation rule underlying radius 0.48 are not reported.
No checkpoint or executable certificate artifact is released in the official record.

evidence.finding: The model/gating and smoothing parameters are partly specified, but the certificate cannot be fully reconstructed from released evidence.
No executable model/certificate artifact is present for comparison with the randomized-smoothing statement.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Input-dependent learned MoE gating described in Section 3.6.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: Not reported in sufficient detail for an artifact-level tie audit.
semantics.weighted_or_selected_output: Routed ensemble feeds a final classification head.
semantics.logit_probability_or_margin_output: Randomized smoothing is defined over the complete final classifier.
semantics.preprocessing_and_perturbation_units: Gaussian randomized smoothing with sigma=0.25; input-unit normalization needed to interpret radius 0.48 is not fully specified.
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Per-input randomized-smoothing certificate for the final classifier.

records.title: Improving the Accuracy-Robustness Trade-Off of Classifiers via Adaptive Smoothing

evidence.finding: The input-dependent alpha theorem is an existence result; the learned mixing network is evaluated with adaptive attacks rather than a numerical certificate.
Numerical certified-radius curves exist for a fixed-alpha subcase, explicitly fixing alpha in the experiment setup; that subcase does not instantiate the included input-dependent guarantee.

evidence.locator: Section 3.1, Theorem 3.5/Theorem 5; Appendix A.2, pp. 8-10 and experiment appendix
evidence.finding: The fixed-alpha bound uses an analytic Gaussian-smoothing Lipschitz constant, while numerical expectations are approximated by 10,000 sampled perturbations without a reported formal sampling confidence construction.
Local Lipschitz behavior used diagnostically is estimated by a PGD-like empirical procedure.

evidence.locator: README, model download sections for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
evidence.finding: The official repository links base classifiers and trained mixing-network checkpoints.
The official repository implements the fixed-alpha Lipschitz and randomized-smoothing certified-radius formulas.

undecidable_or_unoperationalized_premise: Theorem 4.1/Theorem 6 establishes existence of an input-dependent alpha under set-separation conditions; the released learned mixing network is not accompanied by a procedure establishing those conditions for every input.
The public certificate helper operationalizes fixed alpha, not the learned input-dependent alpha artifact.

evidence.finding: Fixed-alpha premises are operationalized, but the adaptive learned-gate guarantee is not fully machine-decidable from the artifact.

mismatches: The released artifact is a learned input-dependent mixing network, while the numerical certificate helper and reported certificate curves use fixed alpha.
The adaptive theorem is existential and does not certify the released learned alpha function.

evidence.finding: The same official repository exposes learned mixing checkpoints and a fixed-alpha certificate helper, making the semantic split directly inspectable.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Input-dependent scalar mixing network alpha(x) between an accurate and a robust classifier.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: Not top-k routing; continuous two-model interpolation.
semantics.preprocessing_and_perturbation_units: CIFAR-10/100; l-infinity attacks for released models and l2/lp certificate theorems as specified per bound.
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Fixed-alpha radius is per input; adaptive-alpha theorem is an existence statement over bounded perturbation sets.

records.title: LAWS: Learning from Actual Workloads Symbolically -- A Self-Certifying Parametrized Cache Architecture for Neural Inference, Robotics, and Edge Deployment

evidence.finding: The paper derives the uniform error bound epsilon_fit + 2 Lambda(W) C_E but does not report a trained-model numerical instantiation of all terms or certified coverage.

Lambda(W) is an analytic product of operator-norm bounds computable from weights, but the paper recommends empirical effective-Lipschitz calibration for production routing and does not provide a fully formal artifact protocol for epsilon_fit.
LAWS is presented as an architecture over an arbitrary base model and expert library; no study-specific trained checkpoint is evaluated as the theorem artifact.
The update and bound are specified in the paper; no official executable certificate repository was linked or located by the cutoff.

undecidable_or_unoperationalized_premise: LayerNorm variance is restricted to an in-distribution condition stated to hold with high probability rather than a machine-checked bounded domain.
Uniform epsilon_fit and Lip(f) <= Lambda(W) are required; the generic PatternRecognize step does not give a complete checking procedure for all proposed expert classes.
Empirical production calibration cannot serve as a sound certificate constant.

evidence.finding: Weight and embedding quantities are computable, but distributional and fitting premises are only partly operationalized.
No released model/certificate artifact was located for semantic comparison.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Any-match trie-radius routing to the nearest matching parametrized expert, otherwise fallback to the base model.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: Single selected expert; equal-distance tie handling is not specified in the inspected theorem text.
semantics.weighted_or_selected_output: Selected expert output or base-model fallback.
semantics.logit_probability_or_margin_output: Vector-output approximation norm, not a classification-margin certificate.
semantics.preprocessing_and_perturbation_units: PLT/trie distance and divergence-token embedding distance.
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Theorem 3 states a uniform output approximation conditional on global Lambda(W), fitting, and expert Lipschitz premises; validity discussion restricts claims to P_M for a LayerNorm premise.

records.title: MetaMoE: Formal Verification of Compositional Robustness and Scalability of Mixture-of-Experts Architecture

evidence.finding: Eight configurations and three perturbation budgets are evaluated; the paper reports numerical router/expert certified robustness results, including 100% router certified robustness accuracy at stated practical bounds.
The numerical certificate uses an alpha-beta-CROWN formal-verification pipeline rather than a theorem constant or sampled Lipschitz provider.

evidence.locator: article page, appendices, and linked resources
evidence.finding: Architecture and ONNX-export details are public, but no paper-specific checkpoint link was located. No author contact was authorized.
The verification pipeline is described in the paper, but no official paper-specific executable certificate repository was located.

undecidable_or_unoperationalized_premise: The released material specifies architecture, raw-logit output, BN folding, and perturbation budgets, but does not release the trained weights required to decide router and expert robustness premises.
No paper-specific verification artifact or exact run configuration was located.

evidence.finding: The model/export semantics are unusually explicit, but the theorem premises cannot all be evaluated without weights and run artifacts.
Paper-level semantics are detailed, but no inspectable paper-specific trained/certificate artifact was located for an artifact/theorem comparison.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Neural router with hard top-1 domain dispatch.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: k=1; tie behavior is not reported in the inspected public evidence.
semantics.logit_probability_or_margin_output: Raw logits, no softmax; Appendix B.
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Per-input compositional robustness requires invariant expert selection and robust selected-expert classification.

records.title: MoET: Mixture of Expert Trees and its Application to Verifiable Reinforcement Learning

evidence.finding: All evaluated hard-routed CartPole policies pass the bounded-state finite-horizon safety check and verification times are reported.
The guarantee is discharged by complete SMT encoding of the policy and environment rather than a numerical robustness-bound constant.
The official repository contains the routed policy artifact used by its verification command.
The official repository exposes the CartPole SMT verification implementation and README command.

evidence.locator: complete verification module together with data/experiments/verified
evidence.finding: The bounded initial state, hard-routed policy, deterministic environment transition, finite horizon, and safety property are represented in the released verification artifact.
The paper's hard MoETH decision-tree routing and closed-loop SMT verification match the released model and cartpole verifier paths.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Hard hierarchical decision-tree router selecting one decision-tree expert.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: Top-1 by deterministic tree predicates; boundary comparison semantics are encoded in SMT.
semantics.logit_probability_or_margin_output: Discrete control action/policy, not classifier logits.
semantics.preprocessing_and_perturbation_units: Bounded CartPole initial-state region and finite execution horizon.
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Closed-loop safety over the encoded bounded initial states and finite horizon.

records.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Mixture of Experts

evidence.locator: Section 3, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1, pp. 4-6; Section 4
evidence.finding: The paper derives Lipschitz bounds for smooth learned routing and fixed-routing linear experts, while experiments report adversarial attacks on V-MoE rather than numerical certificate radii/accuracy.

The bound depends on individual expert Lipschitz constants and a global supremum involving expert outputs/router vectors; no sound computation protocol for these quantities on the evaluated V-MoE is given.
The authors explicitly state that experimental models cannot be released because they were pretrained on proprietary data. No author contact was authorized.
The paper links the V-MoE implementation, but no executable implementation of Lemma 1/Theorem 1 certificate evaluation was located; the formal result remains a paper formula.

undecidable_or_unoperationalized_premise: The experimental checkpoints are unavailable, preventing artifact-specific evaluation of expert Lipschitz constants and router/expert terms.
No procedure is given for soundly computing the global supremum in the smooth-MoE bound on the evaluated model.
The fixed-routing linear-expert theorem does not describe the sparse V-MoE artifact used in experiments.

evidence.finding: Some mathematical objects are explicit, but the evaluated artifact and its required bound quantities cannot be fully decided from released materials.

mismatches: The main learned-routing Lipschitz analysis uses a continuous soft mixture over all experts, while the evaluated V-MoE uses sparse top-k dispatch.
The fixed-routing theorem assumes predetermined routing and linear experts, unlike the evaluated deep V-MoE.
Experimental checkpoints are not released, so no artifact-level theorem instantiation is possible.

evidence.finding: The paper itself separates discontinuous sparse routing from the smooth MoE used for learned-router theory, then evaluates sparse V-MoE with attacks.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Theory: softmax linear continuous weights; experiments: sparse V-MoE routing.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: Sparse definition is top-1 with uniform random choice among tied maxima; experiments use top-2 V-MoE.
semantics.weighted_or_selected_output: Theory includes all-expert weighted output and fixed routing; experiment is sparse selected experts.
semantics.logit_probability_or_margin_output: Function-output Lipschitz analysis and adversarial loss, not a numerical class-margin certificate.
semantics.preprocessing_and_perturbation_units: Norm-bounded adversarial perturbations; experiment-specific V-MoE image attack configuration is reported in Section 4.
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Global Lipschitz bounds for the stated smooth/fixed-routing theoretical models.

records.title: Optimizing Robustness and Accuracy in Mixture of Experts: A Dual-Model Approach

evidence.locator: Section 5, Theorems 5.4-5.5, p. 6; Section 6 and Tables 3-5, pp. 7-9
evidence.finding: The paper states robustness-radius formulas, but its experiments report clean/AutoAttack accuracy and margins; no certified radius or certified-accuracy evaluation of Theorem 5.4/5.5 was located.
The formulas require expert/router Lipschitz quantities L_Ri and r_Ri, but no sound or empirical computation protocol for those quantities is specified.
The official repository provides training/evaluation code but no release checkpoint. No author contact was authorized.
The repository documents training and adversarial evaluation; no implementation of the Theorem 5.4/5.5 certificate was located.

undecidable_or_unoperationalized_premise: The official repository has no trained checkpoint, so model-specific router margins and expert quantities cannot be evaluated.
No computation protocol is supplied for L_Ri and r_Ri.
The theorem's gate semantics and the released hard-argmax router require separate readings rather than a silent identification.

evidence.finding: The affine router boundary is machine-decidable for concrete weights, but no weights are released and the theorem constants remain unoperationalized.

mismatches: The official implementation computes a linear router's logits, takes torch.argmax, and returns only the selected expert output.
Theorem 5.4 is stated using Lipschitz router functions/weights in a weighted MoE output; the paper does not establish its applicability to the released hard-dispatch semantics.
No checkpoint or certificate implementation permits numerical reconciliation.

evidence.finding: The official code is Linear(input, experts) followed by argmax and selected-expert dispatch.
The paper's formal object and assumptions are expressed through input-dependent router weights and their Lipschitz constants.

semantics.router_and_gate_type: Official code: affine input router (Linear(3*size*size, num_experts)) with hard argmax top-1 dispatch.
semantics.top_k_and_tie_semantics: top-1 torch.argmax; first-index tie behavior follows PyTorch implementation but is not discussed in the theorem.
semantics.weighted_or_selected_output: Official code returns selected-expert logits; dual model averages outputs of two separately routed MoEs with fixed alpha.
semantics.logit_probability_or_margin_output: Raw expert logits; attack experiments report accuracy/margins.
semantics.preprocessing_and_perturbation_units: CIFAR-10 image l-infinity attacks in paper configuration; exact normalization-to-pixel-domain mapping requires reproduction audit.
semantics.global_or_local_assumption_domain: Theorem 5.4/5.5 uses local robustness radii conditional on global/local Lipschitz premises and stable router-score separation.
